The petitioner approached the court seeking prayer as under:
"...to issue a Writ, Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Certiorari calling for all connecting records including the impugned Order dated 23.08.2022 in G.O.Ms.No.21 Tribal Welfare (LTR) Department in Revision Petition No.1149 of 2018 passed by the Respondent No.1, dismissing the revision petition of the petitioners, by confirming the orders of the Respondent No.2 in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 dated 15.03.2017 and consequently 4 SN,J wp_3053_2023 quash the impugned G.O.Ms.No.21 Tribal Welfare (LTR) Department, dated 23.08.2022 passed by the Respondent No.1 and the orders of the Respondent No.2 in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 dated 15.03.2017 and pass such other order..."

3. The case of the petitioners as per the averments made by the petitioners in the affidavit filed by the petitioners in support of the present writ petition in brief, is as under:
(i) It is the case of the petitioners that, the then Revenue Divisional Officer and Tribunal, Nirmal for Luxettipetissued certificate of ownership under Section 38-E of A.P (TA) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950 in favour of grandfather of the Petitioners herein as the protected tenant in file No. B5/6513/74 in Form - II in respect of land to an extent of Ac.12-04 gts in Sy.No.137/191 situated at Mandamarri Revenue village, Luxettipet Taluq, Adilabad District (herein after referred to as Subject land).
(ii) Thereafter, the father of the Petitioners No. 1 to 3 namely paid the tax an amount of Rs.1200/- in respect of 38-E vide receipt No.368233, dated 24.6.1973 issued by the then Patwari of the village.

sentences.text: Subsequently, to the death of the petitioners' grandfather and the succeeding possessors, the petitioner Nos. 1 to 5 SN,J wp_3053_2023 6 are the owners and possessors of subject land.
Further the Pahanies for the year 1955-56 to 1972-73 and 1975-76 clearly reflect that the grandfather of the Petitioners was in possession of the land to an extent of Ac.12-04 gts in Sy.No.137/191.

The father of the Respondent No.5 and grandfather of the Respondents No. 6 & 7 was in possession to an extent of Ac. 0-09 gts in Sy.No. 137/191 and some part of the land which was not been cultivated due to various reasons.

(iii) While things stood thus, in the year 2009 the respondents 5 to 7 have applied for grant of pattadar pass book and title deed on extent of Ac 4.10 gts and alleged that 38-E certificate had been issued in favour of the ancestors of the Respondents No.5 to 7, however the same is not supported by records.
The Respondents No.5 to 7 did not take steps for correction of revenue records though their ancestors' names were not mentioned in the records from the year 1974 to 2008.

However, the Mandal Revenue Officers deleted petitioners' names from columns of the possessor and had reduced the ownership over the petitioners subject land from Ac 12-27 gts to Acres Ac 8-17 gts from the year 2008 to 2009.
Moreover, the ancestors of the 6 SN,J wp_3053_2023 respondents were in possession only to an extent of land in Ac.0-09 gts in Sy.No.137/191 of Mandamarri village.

sentences.text: Subsequently, the Respondent No.4 issued Mutation Proceedings No.ROR/14/2009, dated 06.10.2009 (Proceeding No.A/10/884/2009) in favour of Respondents 5 to 7 herein, without any basis, without following the provisions of the A.P. Rights in Land Pattadar Passbook Act 1971 and the rules framed thereunder.

Aggrieved by the same, the Petitioners made an application before Respondent No.4 for cancellation of Proceedings issued in favour of the Respondent Nos.5 to 7 on the ground that the Respondents failed to conduct enquiry and as such the title deed and the pattadar pass books need to be declared as null and void.
But the said application was cancelled by the 4th respondent.

(v) Aggrieved by the action of the respondents, the petitioners filed O.S.No.73/2010 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Mancherial against the Respondents No. 5 to 7 and the same was transferred to the Respondent No.2 and was renumbered as Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 before the Respondent No.2.
However, the Respondent No.2 erroneously dismissed the suit vide order dated 7 SN,J wp_3053_2023 15.03.2017 by stating the respondent nos. 5 to 7 are the possessors of the said property.
(vi) Consequent to the said dismissal, the petitioners filed Revision Petition No.1149 of 2018 before the Respondent No.1 challenging the order dated 15.03.2017 passed by the Respondent No.2.

Subsequently, the petitioner had filed W.P No. 6149 of 2018 challenging the judgment dated 15.03.2017 in case no. A4/CPC/350/2014 and this court vide order dated 26.02.2018 disposed the Petition directing the Respondent No.1 herein to pass appropriate orders on the interlocutory application filed by the Petitioners along with Revision Petition No.1149 of 2018 within a period of 4 weeks from the date of receipt of the order copy.

(vii) It is the specific case of the petitioner that, the 1st respondent passed orders dated 23.08.2022 in Revision Case No.1149 of 2018 dismissing the revision filed by the Petitioners and confirmed the order dated 15.03.2017 in Suit No.A4/CPC/350/2014 passed by the Respondent No.3, mechanically and erroneously placing reliance on the order dated 23.08.2022, the respondent nos. 6 to 8 are trying to dispossess the petitioners from the subject 8 SN,J wp_3053_2023 land.
Aggrieved by the said action of the respondents, the present Writ Petition is filed.

Counter affidavit filed on behalf of the 2nd respondent, in particular, para 6 is extracted hereunder:

"6. In reply to Para no.5, It is submitted that the contention of the petitioners is denied that the Respondent No.4 issued Mutation Proceedings No.ROR/14/2009,
dated 06.10.2009 (Proceeding No.A/10/884/2009) in favour of Respondents 5 to 7 herein, without any basis, without following the provisions of the A.P. Rights in Land Pattadar Passbook Act 1971 and the rules framed thereunder.

As a matter of fact on the basis of 38-E Certificate No.B/6513/74 the respondent no.4 has conducted enquiry and after verifying the connected records and issued mutation proceedings in favour of the respondent no. 5 to 7, rest of the para hence denied.
In reply to para no.6 and 7 it is false to say that the petitioners are in possession and enjoyment of the said land.

It is agreed that the Petitioners filed a civil suit in O.S.No.73/2010 on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Mancherial against the Respondents No. 5 to 7, but the same was transferred to the Respondent No.2 in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nagarjuna Grameena Bank and Others.

Vs. Medi Narayana and Others and therefore the plaint was returned for lack of territorial jurisdiction under Order VII Rule 10(1) of CPC renumbered as case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 before the Respondent No.2.
It is denied that the Respondent No.2 erroneously dismissed the suit vide order dated 15.03.2017.

As such the 2nd respondent 10 SN,J wp_3053_2023 gave opportunity to both the parties, after verification of documentary evidence decided the suit on merit by following the procedure as prescribed under the Civil Procedure Code.
The Writ Petitioners filed Revision Petition No.1149 of 2018 before the Respondent No.1 challenging the order dated 15.03.2017 passed by the Respondent No.2.

The Writ Petitioners have filed W.P.No.1243 of 2018 challenging the action of the Respondent No.4 in dispossessing the Petitioners vide letter dated 06.01.2018, the same was dismissed for default vide order dated 21.06.2019, the other allegations made in para hence denied."

7. The counter affidavit filed on behalf of the 8th and 9th respondent, in particular, para Nos.4, 5, 8 and 10 are extracted hereunder:
"4.

I submit that the writ petitioners filed the revision before the 1st respondent against the judgment dated 15.03.2017 in case No.44/CPC/350/2014 passed by the Sri Durgam Lingaiah And 5 Others vs The State Of Telangana And 9 Others on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155318970/

After hearing and careful observation of the documents and pleadings submitted by all the concerned parties, the 1st respondent herein has dismissed the revision.
Feeling aggrieved by the orders of the 1st respondent, the writ petitioners have filed present writ petition before this Hon'ble Court by suppressing material facts.

5. I submit that the learned lower Court was pleased to dismiss the suit by declaring that the writ petitioners herein 11 SN,J wp_3053_2023 were not in possession and cultivating the suit scheduled property.
The petitioners have not shown any documentary evidence to prove that they are in possession.
Hence, the suit for declaration of title claimed by the petitioner therein not allowed and also perpetual injunction order to the suit land is not tenable.
8. That the Tahsildar had issued Pattadar books to the respondent Nos.5-7 herein and others in the year 2009 and subject land was demarcated by conducting panchanama and boundaries were fixed.

The Tahsildar has issued ROR proceedings vide No.A/ROR/14/2009, dated 6-8-2009.

Mandamari declared that the respondent Nos.5-7 were having physical possession and enjoyment of the subject land.

tenancy and agricultural lands act, 1950 and their names were recorded in revenue records."

8. Counter affidavit filed on behalf of Respondent No.10, in particular, para Nos.4, 5, and 10 are extracted hereunder:
"4.

The Writ Petitioners filed civil suit before 2nd Respondent herein seeking to declare their alleged title to an extent of 12 SN,J wp_3053_2023 Ac.12-04 Gts in Sy No:137/191 in Buradagudem Village, Mandamuri Mandal, Mancherial District.
The Writ Petitioners sought for Perpetual Injunction against the Respondents 5 to 9 herein.
I was not arrayed as defendant despite my right, title and possession to the subject land.
I was not even aware of the said proceedings before the 2nd Respondent herein.
Therefore I did not have an opportunity to contest the matter before 2nd Respondent herein.
The Respondents 5 to 9 herein contested the matter.

Based on the said contest, 2nd Respondent herein dismissed the said suit holding that the Respondents 5 to 9 herein are having title over Ac. 4-10 Gts out of Ac. 12-04 Gts in the suit schedule property and the said trial court finding was that the remaining Ac.8-17 Gts belonged to my mother Pusukuru Buchamma, from whom as a sole legal heir I devolved the same.
Therefore when I came to know about the said legal proceedings behind my back I got impleaded before 1st Respondent herein.
5. Aggrieved by the said Judgment of the 2nd Respondent herein the Writ Petitioners approached the 1st respondent.

The 1st Respondent vide its G.O.Ms No.21 dt.23/08/2022 upheld the Judgment of the 2nd Respondent herein while dismissing Sri Durgam Lingaiah And 5 Others vs The State Of Telangana And 9 Others on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155318970/

sentences.text: the claim of the Writ Petitioners.
10. The fundamental basis for the Writ Petitioners claim rests upon the alleged 38-E Certificate in favour of Kota Lasumaiah.

The finding of the trial court and revisional authority that this Kota Lasumaiah is not Durgam Lasumaiah, therefore the very foundation is built on a false claim, they cannot seek the discretionary 13 SN,J wp_3053_2023 indulgence of this Hon'ble Court under Article 226 of Constitution of India.

The Primary authority Tahsildar - Respondent No: 4 specifically gave a report to the Respondent No. 3 - R.D.O that the total extent of land in Sy No.137 of Mandamuri Village is Ac.14-33 Gts, and the manipulated and fabricated 38-E certificates cropped up to Ac. 27-27Gts.
Therefore 38-E certificates are bogus and the said certificates cannot be relied upon as they are not authentic and real.

The said 4th Respondent Tahsildar further stated that out of Ac.14-33Gts, an extent of Ac.2-06 Gts was acquired by M/s. Orient Cement Company, Devapur for laying Railway Line to its factory, and that the Durgam Mallaiah's family took the land acquisition compensation to the said land.

Further an extent of Ac.4-10 Gts was implemented in favour of Segyam family as 38-E Tenants and the remaining Ac.8-17Gts is held by me having succeeded the same from my mother Smt. Pusukuru Buchamma, who is the original pattadar of the entire land."

sentences.text:
It is the specific case of the petitioners before the primary authority that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of the land in survey No.137/191 to an extent of Ac.12.04 gts., situated at Mandamarri Revenue Village and Mandal, and the petitioners came to know that the Proceeding No.ROR/14/2009 dated 06.10.2009 (Procgs No.A/10884/2009) on the file of Tahsildar,
Mandamarri were wrongly issued in favour of the defendants thereunder 15 SN,J wp_3053_2023 in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 and the petitioners are the illiterate rustic villagers, who were unable to protect their possession over the subject suit land property and that the mandatory provision under Section 5 (3) of the Act had been violated by respondent No.4 since no notice had been issued to the petitioners while effecting mutation in favour of Respondent Nos.5 to 7 amounting to violation of principles of natural justice and though the said plea had been specifically urged by the petitioners both the Primary Authority and the Revisional Authority, failed to consider the same.
11.

A bare perusal of the order impugned dated 23.08.2022 passed by the 1st respondent does not indicate any reasons in dismissing the revision petition filed by the petitioner Nos.1 to 6 and the 1st respondent mechanically confirmed the orders of the Additional Agent to Government and Project Officer, ITDA Utnoor, Adilabad in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 dated 15.03.2017 simply holding that the revision petitioners failed to prove their claim in the lower Court in Suit No.A4/CPC/350/2014 before the 16 SN,J wp_3053_2023 Additional Agent to Government and Project Officer, ITDA Utnoor and also before the Government in the revision petition.

12. A bare perusal of the impugned order dated 23.08.2022 passed in G.O.Ms.No.21, Tribal Welfare (LTR) Department in Revision Petition No.1149/2018 by the 1st respondent dismissing the Revision Petition filed by the petitioners duly confirming the orders of the 2nd respondent in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014, dated 15.03.2017, clearly indicates that the 1st respondent failed to consider the specific pleas put forth by the petitioners in the Revision Petition since the order impugned does not indicate framing of any specific issues by the 1st respondent herein evidencing consideration of the specific pleas put forth by the petitioner in the revision petition, nor any specific findings recorded based on the said specific issues framed, in adjudicating the subject issue.
As borne on record the impugned order dated 23.08.2022 passed by the 1st respondent is bereft of reasons.

This Court opines that without going into the merits of the rival contentions put forth by all the learned counsel on record, in the interest of Justice, it is just and necessary to remit the matter back to the 1st respondent herein to decide the entire issue afresh again by giving an opportunity of personal hearing to all concerned for passing of appropriate reasoned orders, in accordance to law,
in conformity with principles of natural justice.
14. This Court opines that the Judgments relied upon by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.8, 9 and 10 do not apply to the facts of the present case.

15. Taking into consideration:
Sri Durgam Lingaiah And 5 Others vs The State Of Telangana And 9 Others on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155318970/
8 (a) The averments made in the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the 2nd respondent and the counter affidavit filed on behalf of respondent Nos.8, 9 and 10,
(b) The interim orders of this Court dated 03.02.2023, passed in favour of the petitioners vide W.P.No.3053 of 2023, (referred to and extracted above), which are in force as on date, 18 SN,J wp_3053_2023 (c) Duly considering the Judgments relied upon by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners referred to above at para '9' of the present order, The Writ Petition is allowed, the order impugned dated 23.08.2022 passed by the 1st respondent is set aside and the matter is remitted to the 1st respondent to decide the revision dated 14.02.2018 preferred by the petitioners aggrieved against the order of Additional Agent to Government and Project Officer, ITDA Utnoor in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 dated 15.03.2017, in accordance to law, in conformity with principles of natural justice by issuing Notices to all concerned, within a period of eight (08) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order and pass appropriate orders by giving adequate reasons and duly communicate the same to the petitioners and to all concerned.

(ii) The Judgment dated 26.03.2009 reported in (2009) 4 Supreme Cases 240 in "Chairman, Disciplinary 14 SN,J wp_3053_2023 Authority, Rani Lakshmi Bai Kshetriya Gramin Bank v.
Jagdish Sharan Varsheny and others", [paras 5, 8, 9].
(iii) The Judgment dated 31.03.2010 reported in Manu/AP/0050/2010 in "K.Santha Kumar v.
Revenue Divisional Officer and Others", [para 11].
(iv) The Judgment dated 04.04.2005 reported in Manu/SC/0257/2005 in "State of N.C.T. of Delhi and Others v. Sanjeev", [para 16].
(v) The Judgment dated 19.01.2022 reported in Manu/TL/0065/2022 in "President, Healthcare Reforms Doctors Assn. and Ors. V. Spl. Chief Secy., Health, Medical Family Welf. Dept and Ors.",
[para 18].
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the specific case of the petitioners before the primary authority that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of the land in survey No.137/191 to an extent of Ac.12.04 gts., situated at Mandamarri Revenue Village and Mandal, and the petitioners came to know that the Proceeding No.ROR/14/2009 dated 06.10.2009 (Procgs No.A/10884/2009) on the file of Tahsildar,
Mandamarri were wrongly issued in favour of the defendants thereunder 15 SN,J wp_3053_2023 in Case No.A4/CPC/350/2014 and the petitioners are the illiterate rustic villagers, who were unable to protect their possession over the subject suit land property and that the mandatory provision under Section 5 (3) of the Act had been violated by respondent No.4 since no notice had been issued to the petitioners while effecting mutation in favour of Respondent Nos.5 to 7 amounting to violation of principles of natural justice and though the said plea had been specifically urged by the petitioners both the Primary Authority and the Revisional Authority, failed to consider the same.
11.
14. This Court opines that the Judgments relied upon by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.8, 9 and 10 do not apply to the facts of the present case.
